- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean by > 2% over 3–5 periods, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast for next period.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 65% of 30-day average, model tends to overreact; apply downward bias correction.
